engagement_title: Isla Verde signage refresh: recover a foil stamped monogram off a printed brochure, build a facility pictogram set from its own construction, author the directional panels at true cut size, rebuild the 2016 door plate into a live twenty four record run, and hand the sign shop a schedule it can work from
vertical: Hospitality and travel, a forty two room independent coastal resort refinishing its corridors and replacing a failed 2016 sign programme (Gulf coast, Florida)
real_brief_anchor: The ledger row for VECTOR-05 carries an empty real_brief_anchors array, so the anchor is the recurring posted commission this concept was carved from rather than a single quoted post. It is one of the most common shapes on Upwork and Freelancer.com in the hospitality category: a property posts under a title of the form 'wayfinding and signage design for boutique resort' or 'recreate our logo from a printed brochure, vector needed', and the body always contains the same three admissions, that the original designer is unreachable, that the only surviving artwork is printed on something, and that the sign fabricator needs files by a date, with 'vector', 'editable', 'exact sizes' and 'we need our actual logo, not a new one' recurring almost verbatim. The ledger's own one_line_ask is quoted into the client voice here: we are refreshing signage across our resort and only have a printed brochure showing our old monogram, recover it cleanly and build a coordinated wayfinding system, all as editable artwork our sign shop can cut. The triage verdict on the row is STRENGTHEN, and two things had to change to meet the standard. First, the ledger's own 'mounted-panel mockup on a wall photo' is photo compositing, which is not connector work, so it is re-carved as what a real signage engagement actually hands over instead: the property's own location photography brought to one look for the standards document, plus a licensed camera scale frame for the mount points the property never photographed. Second, as carved the row sat almost entirely on one surface. The door plate is the part of a wayfinding programme that is genuinely a volume run, twenty four facilities at one plate per door, and the property already owns the 2016 press artwork the current plates were cut from, which is exactly the input a record per page run needs and exactly why the fixings still line up.
client_one_liner: The only place our monogram still exists at any quality is a foil stamp on the cover of a brochure we printed in 2019, and the sign shop needs artwork by the end of next month.
client_brief:
Isla Verde, signage refresh

We are a forty two room property on the Gulf coast, family owned, three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night. Our guests are thirty to fifty five and they come here because it is quiet.

Our signs are a mess. The system went in around 2016 with a local shop that has since closed, pieces of it have been replaced by whoever was available, and the door plates are chipped. We are refinishing the corridors this winter and the sign shop needs artwork by the end of next month.

The problem is our monogram. The only place it still exists at any quality is the cover of a brochure we printed in 2019, stamped in foil. Our designer moved abroad and nothing ever came back from her. We need the monogram back as artwork a sign shop can cut at any size, and it has to be our monogram, not a new one drawn to look like it.

Then the system. Directional signs for the corridors and for the garden path. A small set of facility symbols, eight of them, that look like they were drawn by whoever drew the monogram rather than bought from a catalogue. A door plate for every room and facility, twenty four of them, in English and Spanish, at the same size and printed the same way as the ones on the doors now so the existing fixings still line up. And a schedule the sign shop can work from: every panel, its size, its copy, where it goes.

We are also sending photographs of the walls the panels go on, and of four signs already up that the owner likes.

We want the standards written down as well, so the next person who orders a sign does not invent something.

How it should feel: quiet. A lot of empty space, one or two greys, the monogram. Our guests notice when a place is shouting at them. Nothing that looks like an airport or a car park.
price_band_and_audience: Upscale independent resort, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night, guest thirty to fifty five and travelling for quiet. The band is load-bearing and it decides the whole system. At this tier the signage is restrained: generous clear space, one or two close greys rather than contrast for its own sake, a delicate monogram, type set small and confidently, symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark. A budget motel system doing the same job would correctly be louder, denser, higher contrast and larger in type, because it has to be read fast by someone who does not want to be there, and shipping that treatment here reads as a highway property and undercuts the rate. Push the other way into near invisible pale on pale and the system stops doing the one thing signage exists to do, which at this tier is worse than looking cheap, because a guest who cannot find the spa asks at the desk and the quiet is what they paid for. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A real posted job of this shape runs 2,000 to 5,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: Independent upscale coastal resort refreshing its corridor and garden wayfinding and its room signage.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Family owned, Gulf coast of Florida, a forty two room property with corridors, a garden path and about twenty four rooms and facilities.
brand_identity.about: Isla Verde is a family owned resort on the Gulf coast where guests come for quiet. Forty two rooms, refinished corridors and a garden that people walk slowly. The signage is being rebuilt this winter so the property reads as calmly as it feels, with the house monogram carried consistently from the door plates to the directional panels.
brand_identity.audience: Independent leisure travellers thirty to fifty five paying for calm, who notice when a place is shouting and value being able to find their way without being told loudly.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Upscale independent, rooms three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty a night. Signage should read at that tier: generous clear space, delicate marks, confidence rather than contrast for its own sake.
brand_identity.typography: A fine interlocking monogram set small and confidently, paired with a quiet, well spaced text face. Type kept modest and legible, never large or emphatic. Facility symbols drawn with the same hand as the mark.
brand_identity.voice: Understated, warm, precise. It gives directions without raising its voice. Example line: The spa is along the garden path, second door on the left.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: No monogram source file survives. The designer moved abroad and nothing was handed back. The only decent record of the mark is a foil stamp on the cover of a brochure printed in 2019. The 2016 sign shop that cut the current door plates has since closed, though its press artwork for the plates is still on file.
brand_identity.values: A sense of quiet that guests can navigate, and a written standard so the next person who orders a sign does not invent something new.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_brochure_cover.jpg (4032 x 3024)
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of the 2019 printed brochure lying on a desk, the monogram foil stamped on uncoated cream stock: an interlocking I and V inside a fine oval rule with a small palm frond at the join.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only decent picture of the monogram we still have. It is stamped in foil so it catches the light."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Foil has no single ink value. The same stroke reads dark on one flank and near white specular on the other, so an ink level selection returns a plausible looking partial with whole strokes missing and no indication that anything is absent. The mark is also stamped small on the cover, so whatever survives the trace carries only the detail that was in those pixels, and the oval rule and the counters of the interlocked letters are the first things to close at the size the mark actually reproduces on a pale panel.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_locations/ (10 frames, phone)
assets_supplied.kind: Phone photographs of the corridor and garden mount points, taken by the duty manager over two days.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Where the panels go. Taken on my phone, sorry about the quality."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the ten are the same corridor shot from opposite ends and three facilities on the schedule have no frame at all, which no filename reveals. The phone's automatic white balance also renders three genuinely different wall finishes as the same neutral, so the frames cannot be trusted to say how a panel will sit against the wall it mounts to.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_doorplate_2016.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The closed sign shop's press artwork for the plate currently on every door, the file the existing plates were cut from.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What is on the doors now. The fixings are drilled for this size so it cannot change."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The name line sits in a fixed measure frame sized to the longest facility name the property had in 2016. A longer name does not spill, reflow or overset at trim, it simply stops rendering partway through, so the merged page looks entirely correct at page thumbnail scale and the loss is only visible at the plate's real size. The bilingual second line shares the same story as the name.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_schedule.csv
assets_supplied.kind: Twenty four facilities: number, English name, Spanish name, floor, panel type, mount height.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Every door and facility, with both languages. The Spanish came from our front office manager."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Three of the English names and five of the Spanish are materially longer than anything the 2016 plate ever carried, two rows are the same facility on two floors with identical copy, and one facility's name cannot fit the plate at any legible size, which is a decision to escalate to the owner rather than a problem to solve quietly.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_existing_signs/ (4 frames)
assets_supplied.kind: Photographs of four signs already on the property that the owner likes and wants the new system to sit with.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "These four are fine. Whatever you do should look like it belongs with them."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two are from the 2016 programme and two survive from an earlier one with a noticeably heavier stroke and a different corner language, and nothing labels which is which, so matching all four means matching two incompatible systems and the owner has not noticed that they are two.

assets_supplied.name: islaverde_signshop_note.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The new fabricator's requirements: substrate and finish, the panel sizes they cut, minimum legible type height at their stated viewing distances, and clear space at the panel edge.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "What the new sign shop sent over when we asked what they need."

acceptance_bar: The monogram is placeable scalable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it, and it is still recognisably this property's monogram rather than a new mark drawn to resemble it.
The monogram holds at the size it actually reproduces on each panel, with the oval rule and the interlocked counters open rather than closed, judged on the panel ground and not at full canvas.

The eight pictograms are drawn from the monogram's own construction, one stroke language, one corner language, one terminal, and each is drawn for the size it is placed at rather than one drawing scaled to two sizes.

Every panel is authored at the fabricator's true cut size in real physical units, with the stated clear space honoured and type at or above the fabricator's minimum legible height for its viewing distance.
No artwork runs off a panel's cut edge anywhere in the delivered document, on any panel, including panels that cannot be previewed as a rendered page.

Twenty four door plates, one facility per page, page count equal to row count, at the same trim as the 2016 plate so the existing fixings still line up, and every name on every plate readable in full at plate size in both languages.
Any facility whose name cannot fit the plate at a legible size is named to the owner as a decision, not silently abbreviated and not silently truncated.
Per record files handed to the fabricator carry the facility they claim to carry, and the delivered set is rendered at press resolution rather than at screen scale.

The panels, the plate face and the schedule sit in ONE working file with live editable text and the monogram and pictograms as real vector shapes, delivered with the self contained source it was built from.
One type system across every panel with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer and the actual weight used, and a stated minimum size below which the system must not be set.
The system reads as a three hundred and eighty to six hundred and fifty dollar property: quiet, spare, close greys. Loud, dense and high contrast fails even if every measurement is correct.

This is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout, absolute physical units resolve exactly, a real table survives as a real table, and inline SVG arrives as native editable vector, which is what lets the fabricator receive a system rather than a picture of one.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, read the fabricator's note and the schedule, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface.
trajectory.judgement: The panels and the standards are an authored fixed canvas document because the property will order signs from them for years, the plates are a record per page run because the fixings fix the trim and there are twenty four of them, and the monogram is recovery work that everything else depends on. The brief pins all three, so there is nothing to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: A manifest keyed by role, because the ten location frames are named by phone timestamp and nothing else will identify them later.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Look at the brochure cover, all ten location frames and the four existing signs, and triage: how the foil behaves across the stamp, which mount points are actually photographed, which two frames are the same wall, and which of the four existing signs belong to which system.
trajectory.judgement: The owner believes the four signs are one family and that ten frames cover ten mount points. Only the pictures can settle either, and reading the schedule against filenames is not the same as reading it against the frames.
trajectory.produces: A triage note covering foil behaviour, frame to facility reconciliation and the two stroke languages in the existing signs.

trajectory.action: Straighten the location frames that sit off level, before any bounds decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Recover the monogram: an ink level selection worded from the stamp's own visual properties rather than from the stock it sits on, the correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed. Then look at what came back at the size it will actually reproduce, on a pale ground.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes the stamp and not the board, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour trace or the colour accurate knockout plate is the deliverable the sign shop can cut.
trajectory.produces: A candidate monogram master with its recovery route recorded and inspected at reproduction size.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit. Set a minimum size against the fabricator's legible height.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a quiet upscale property and against a fabricator's stated viewing distances. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight per role, plus a stated minimum size.

trajectory.action: Author the eight facility pictograms as inline SVG geometry built from the recovered monogram's own stroke weight, terminal and corner language. Lay two directions, a monoline construction and a solid glyph construction, and pick one.
trajectory.judgement: The pick is argued against the monogram's own construction and against the band, not chosen freely. Bought in looking symbols are the specific failure the owner named.
trajectory.produces: Eight pictograms in the chosen direction, with the rejected direction kept for the handover.

trajectory.action: Set the panel system: sizes taken from the fabricator's cut list, clear space from their note, and the value relationship between panel ground, monogram, pictogram and type judged against the band.
trajectory.judgement: At this tier restraint is the design, but a system nobody can read sends the guest to the desk. Where that line sits is the central art direction call in the engagement.
trajectory.produces: A written panel system: sizes, clear space, values, type scale and minimum size.

trajectory.action: Author the directional panels and the door plate face at true physical size in absolute units, every SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, each pictogram placed at the size its panel actually needs.
trajectory.judgement: An auto sized or right anchored wrapper collapses and throws its contents off the cut edge, so everything is anchored and sized. A corridor directional and a door plate are two different optical problems, not one drawing at two scales.
trajectory.produces: Panel and plate roots at true cut sizes.

trajectory.action: Author the signage schedule as a real table in the same document, and the standards pages naming the type system, clear space, minimum size and the monogram's rules of use.
trajectory.judgement: The schedule is what the fabricator actually works from, so it has to carry panel, size, copy in both languages and location, and it has to survive as a table rather than as a picture of one.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying panels, plate face, pictogram sheet, schedule and standards, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, upload the HTML and export by URL.
trajectory.judgement: The readiness check runs before every export and every retry, and the payload travels by uploaded URL because inlined photography passes the inline threshold immediately.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document carrying every root.

trajectory.action: Verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first artboard, and parse the returned per canvas markup for every other root, element by element.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop and every normalisation this importer performs returns success with no warning of any kind, and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at one panel is not looking at the system.
trajectory.produces: An inspected first artboard and a per canvas markup audit covering every panel, the plate face, the pictogram sheet and the schedule table.

trajectory.action: Bring the location frames to one house target for the standards document, one call per frame, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: They were shot over two days on a phone that made its own white balance decisions, so one batched parameter set is exactly wrong. The target is a set that looks like one property, not ten good frames.
trajectory.produces: A graded location set at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Search short generic queries for the three mount points nobody photographed, filter to photography, exclude generative tech candidates, license and download at full resolution, and bring the frame to the same target.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the house target rather than the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera scale frame graded into the same set.

trajectory.action: Convert the 2016 plate artwork, export the interchange file, and read what the conversion actually exposes as addressable frames and what the plate's story text actually says, then build the field map from that and prepare the merge template.
trajectory.judgement: What a press PDF exposes is a property of how it was set, not of how the plate looks on the door. Promising a field map before looking is promising something nobody has checked.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory, the plate's true story text, and a prepared merge template.

trajectory.action: Merge the twenty four facilities one record per page, render at press resolution at the 2016 trim, produce per record files for the fabricator with identity guaranteed per call rather than by position in a returned list, and read the plates at plate size.
trajectory.judgement: The fixings fix the trim, so the plate cannot be resized to solve a copy problem. Reading twenty four pages at page thumbnail scale is not reading them.
trajectory.produces: A twenty four page press file at the existing trim plus per record files, with the plates actually inspected at size.

trajectory.action: Create the direction selects board, add the graded location set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-sending only the entries the response names as failed, then write the standards note and the schedule handover.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector system is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to be specific enough that the next person who orders a sign does not invent something, which is what the owner actually asked for.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written standards and schedule handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a foil stamp actually gives back. Foil has no single ink value: across one stroke it reads dark where it turns away from the light and near white and specular where it turns toward it, and the cream stock sits between the two. An ink level selection therefore returns a partial that looks entirely plausible, complete in some strokes and absent in others, with no count, no confidence and no flag saying anything is missing. Which strokes survive is a property of how the brochure happened to be lying when the photograph was taken. Only after the trace, viewed at the size the mark reproduces on a pale panel rather than at full canvas, does it become visible whether the oval rule is continuous, whether the interlock still reads as two letters, and whether the counters have closed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it: the tracing tool takes no options at all, the only lever is what the raster prep hands it, and no reading of the photograph at preview scale distinguishes a specular flank from missing artwork. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the monogram is stamped in foil and catches the light. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different derivation, selecting the cream stock and inverting, or filling a knockout plate against the inverted mask and tracing that instead of tracing the mask, and each of those is a different artwork with a different route.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-derive the monogram through a different route, judge the result again at reproduction size on the panel ground rather than at full canvas, and where a hairline cannot be recovered at all decide whether to author that element as path geometry consistent with what did survive or to tell the owner the rule cannot be recovered, then re-place the master everywhere it appears.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A monogram that looks correct in the handover file and closes into a solid blob on every door plate and every corridor panel on the property, delivered against a brief whose first sentence is that it has to still be their monogram.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: How the importer normalises a monoline pictogram, and whether a symbol drawn for a corridor panel is still a symbol on a door plate. The pictograms are authored as unfilled stroked paths, which is the correct construction for a cut sign system, and the importer recomputes path geometry from the drawing's own coordinate space into rendered canvas units. Whether the stroke survives as a stroke, and whether its weight is recomputed with the geometry or carried across unchanged, is reported nowhere and is knowable only from the returned markup. If the weight does not travel with the geometry, the symbol placed at plate size arrives carrying the corridor panel's weight and reads as a filled blot while the corridor panel itself is perfect, and the document's rendition returns the first artboard only, so the plate face and every panel after the first cannot be looked at any other way.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the normalisation happens at import and the import is downstream of every authoring decision, and doing it right the first time presumes knowing which of several plausible constructions survives, which no tool reports and no checklist enumerates. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks only for eight symbols that look like the monogram drew them, and the acceptance line about drawing each pictogram for its own size is the client's craft requirement, not a disclosure about an importer. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is to author a separate optical cut of each symbol for each destination size, which is a different set of drawings, not the same drawing re-exported.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Draw a second optical cut of all eight symbols for the small destination, re-decide the panel value relationships now that the small symbol's weight has changed, re-author, re-upload, re-run the readiness check, re-export, and audit every root from the returned markup rather than from the first artboard.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twenty four door plates and every secondary panel carrying eight filled blots where the facility symbols should be, in a document that reported success at every step and whose one previewable page looks immaculate.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the plate does not overflow, it stops. The name line on the 2016 artwork sits in a fixed measure frame sized to the longest name the property had in 2016, and a longer name does not spill, reflow, overset or flag: it simply stops rendering partway through, so the merged page is well formed, correctly laid out and quietly short. At page thumbnail scale twenty four plates all look right. Which of the twenty four are short depends on the interaction between the actual string, the face and the weight finally chosen, so it cannot be predicted from the data file, and the Spanish line and the English line fail at different lengths. The multi record raster route compounds it by returning files in an order that does not match the labels, so naming a per record file by its position asserts an identity that was never checked.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the frame's measure comes from artwork the property already owns and cannot be resized because the fixings are drilled, and the truncation point is a function of the type system, which is a later decision. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the plates must be the same size as the ones on the doors now, and the acceptance line about names reading in full is the client's requirement, not a warning that a frame truncates. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a decision, either a per facility naming convention agreed against the property's own signage language, or a change to the type system that then propagates back through every panel in the document, plus one name escalated to the owner because it cannot fit at any legible size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read all twenty four plates at plate size in both languages, decide per affected facility between abbreviation, a type change that reaches back into the whole system, and escalation, then rebuild the mapping and re-merge, and confirm per record identity through a route that guarantees it rather than through the order of a returned list.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Plates screwed to doors reading Coastal Terrace and Suns and Pabellon de Tenis y Tie, cut in the fabricator's substrate at the property's expense, with the merged file having reported success and looked correct on screen.

deliverables.name: Recovered Isla Verde monogram master
deliverables.spec: The 2019 foil stamp recovered as placeable scalable vector geometry with a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, the oval rule continuous and the interlock still reading as two letters at the size it actually reproduces on a pale panel and reversed. Delivered with a stated recovery route and, where an element could not be recovered from the photograph, an explicit statement of what was authored instead and why.

deliverables.name: Facility pictogram set, eight symbols at two optical cuts
deliverables.spec: Eight facility symbols as editable vector geometry built from the monogram's own stroke weight, terminal and corner language, drawn at each destination size rather than one drawing scaled, in one chosen direction with the rejected direction shown and the pick argued against the monogram's construction and the band.

deliverables.name: Directional panels and door plate face at true cut size
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying the corridor and garden directional panels and the plate face at the fabricator's true cut sizes in real physical units, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the monogram and the symbols as real vector shapes, the fabricator's clear space honoured, type at or above their minimum legible height, and no artwork running off any cut edge on any panel. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from.

deliverables.name: Twenty four door plates as a live run

decision_gates: Which deliverables need an authored fixed canvas document at true cut sizes and which need a record per page run, given that only one surface composes free form layout and only one produces volume personalisation.
Selection wording on the foil stamp: naming the brochure or the stock takes the board, naming the stamp's own visual properties takes the mark, and neither route reports what it left behind.
Which recovery route the monogram needs, and what to do about an element the photograph simply does not contain: author it consistently, or tell the owner it cannot be recovered.
Whether the four existing signs are one family or two, and which of the two the new system should sit with, when the owner has not noticed they are two.
Monoline construction versus solid glyph for the pictograms, argued against the monogram's own construction rather than chosen freely.
How much contrast the panels carry. At this band restraint is the design and a guest who cannot find the spa is the worse failure, so where that line sits is the central call.
Whether a symbol drawn for a corridor panel can be the same drawing on a door plate, or whether the small destination needs its own optical cut.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a quiet upscale property and a fabricator's minimum legible height, plus the real numeric weight per family.
What to do with three facilities that have no photograph and two frames that are the same wall, when the schedule asserts ten mount points.
Per facility naming when the plate's measure is fixed by fixings already drilled: abbreviate to a convention, change the type system and propagate it back through every panel, or escalate.
How per record identity is guaranteed for the fabricator, given that the order of a returned list is not evidence of what a file contains.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the photographs into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of resort signs. IDENTITY: this is the monogram a designer made for this property and stamped on a 2019 brochure, and the client's own sentence is that it has to be their monogram and not a new one drawn to look like it, which is exactly what a generated mark is. SPEC: the fabricator cuts to a fixed size list with a stated clear space and a minimum legible type height, the door plates must land at the 2016 trim because the fixings are already drilled, and there are twenty four of them with two languages each, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the property will order signs from this system for years and explicitly asked for standards so the next person does not invent something, so a flat picture of a sign is the opposite of the deliverable. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did the foil actually give the oval rule back, is the symbol on the plate still a symbol, does this plate say Coastal Terrace or Coastal Terrace and Suns.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, fill_area, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, auto_straighten and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and an ink level mark was recovered off a photographed printed surface with counters correctly excluded. The recovery checkpoint rests on documented findings rather than assumptions: the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry (the same photograph returning either a 154,926 pixel object mask or a 9,372 pixel ink mask depending only on wording), the silent partial selection on compound marks that drops elements while succeeding, the missing viewBox, and the opaque full canvas path at index zero. EXPRESS: multiple roots at mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, absolute physical units resolve exactly at 96 dpi (210mm by 297mm to 794 by 1123 px, with mm child coordinates converted), a table survives as a real table with per cell text and strokes, and inline SVG becomes native editable vector with path data recomputed from the drawing's coordinate space into rendered pixels, which is the exact mechanism the pictogram checkpoint turns on. The rendition preview is documented as first artboard only, which is why verification is split between the rendition and the returned per canvas markup, and the right anchored auto sized wrapper collapse is a verified failure that the acceptance bar scores. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB threshold immediately. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as generator and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified headless and synchronous, one record per page for PDF is verified with page count equal to row count, frame granularity from a PDF is verified as not under the author's control, per record identity is taken through the verified createSeparateFiles or recordRange routes because multi record raster URLs came back reversed, and press resolution is taken through document_render_layout because merge output silently ignores resolution. No bleed is claimed, since a PDF derived template carries none, and pdfPreset is never passed. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, including the non standard numeric weights and the display cut reached by its own slug. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, a real full resolution licensed JPEG, and boards persisting with a cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no photo compositing of any kind including the re-carved wall mockup, no upscaling, no OCR, no text to image, no generative fill, no variable QR, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
